summary: Akio Tanabe specializes in Indology and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1985–1994) and later held posts as Associate Professor at Kyoto University (~1998–2008) and at the University of Tokyo (~2017).
Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1934) and held a post there as team leader (班長).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. He served as Professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1975) and held posts at Waseda, Rissho, Komazawa, and ICPBS.

Akira Miyaji specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and D.Litt at Nagoya University, where he became Emeritus Professor (~2004), and held posts at Hirosaki University and Ryukoku University (~2004–2015).

Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral course at Hokkaido University (~1969–1974), served there as an assistant (~1974–1978), and was attested as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College in 1999.

Akira Omine (1929–2018) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1949–1953), he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Ryukoku University, and Osaka University, where he was named professor emeritus.

Akira Onda (1925–2015) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1950) and held posts at Toyo University (~1960–1995), Kawamura Gakuen Women's University, and the University of Tokyo (Professor Emeritus).

Akira Sadakata specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and at the University of Paris. His main career was at Tokai University as associate professor, professor, and emeritus professor.

Akira Saito specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and earned a PhD from the Australian National University. He held posts at Mie University, the University of Tokyo, and ICPBS.

Akira Shimada specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, supervised by Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali, and held posts at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1957–1962), where he spent his career as assistant, associate professor, professor (~1977–2005), and president (1991–1994).

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) was a Sinologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1981–1991) and later held posts at Tokyo Woman's Christian University and Meikai University.

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying under Akira Hirakawa, Naoshiro Tsuji, J.W. de Jong, and A.L. Basham. He held posts at ANU, Soka University, and served as Director of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Akitoshi Saito is a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who held posts at Taisho University as a professor (attested 1982) and emeritus professor (attested 2014).

Alan Fox specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University (attested 1988) and held posts as Professor (1992) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2013–2014) at the University of Delaware.

Alan Gerard Wagner specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2008) under doctoral supervisor Parimal G. Patil, also studying under Robert M. Gimello, Charles Hallisey, Carl Bielefeldt, and Masatoshi Nagatomi.

Alan Sponberg specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing his PhD at the University of British Columbia. He held faculty posts as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and in religious studies at Stanford University (attested 1988).
Alan Watts (1915–1973) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He was educated at St Hugh's School and The King's School Canterbury (~1928–1932).

Alasdair Urquhart specializes in philosophy. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1963–1967) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1967–1973), and held a post at the University of Toronto (~1973–2012).

Alastair Gornall specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013) and held posts at SOAS University of London (~2015–2019) and Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2016).
